title: Observer Maxwell equations and conserved source charge

items.title: Observer Maxwell equations and conserved source charge
items.statement:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth ($C^\infty$), Hausdorff, second-countable,
boundaryless, oriented, time-oriented four-manifold with Lorentz metric of
signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and oriented volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Use SI units:
$c>0$ has exact defining value $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; its
identification as the vacuum light/clock conversion is adopted in this
framework, not derived here. The constant $\mu_0>0$ has units
$\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined in the revised SI; set
$\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$. The manifold
orientation is independent of the time orientation. Let $\mathcal D\subseteq M$
be the open field domain. Let $F$ be a smooth real two-form with components in
tesla, and let $j$ be a smooth vector field whose components have units
$\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$, both on $\mathcal D$. An **observer field** is a smooth
future-directed vector field $n$ with $g(n,n)=-1$; no
hypersurface-orthogonality or global inertial chart is assumed. On decomposable
$k$-covectors define
$\langle\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k,\beta_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\beta_k\rangle_g:=\det(g^{-1}(\alpha_i,\beta_j))$ and extend bilinearly. Define the Hodge star by
$\alpha\wedge *\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$ and define
insertion by $(i_X\omega)(Y_1,\ldots,Y_{k-1})=\omega(X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_{k-1})$.
The observer fields are the spatial covectors
$E_a:=cF_{ab}n^b=-c(i_nF)_a$ and
$B_a:= -(*F)_{ab}n^b=(i_n*F)_a$. Antisymmetry makes both covectors spatial,
that is, they annihilate $n$. In a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with
time axis $n$ (an ordered basis with metric matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$), let $\delta_{ij}$ be the Euclidean spatial metric and let
$\varepsilon_{ijk}$ be the alternating symbol with $\varepsilon_{123}=+1$;
at an event write $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\varepsilon_{ijk}B_k$ for the
tetrad components at that event. Define the local
charge and current densities by $\rho:=j^0/c$ and $J^i:=j^i$, so
$[\rho]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}$ and $[J^i]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$. For spatial
components define $\nabla\cdot X:=\sum_i\partial_iX_i$ and
$(\nabla\times X)_k:=\varepsilon_{kij}\partial_iX_j$. Coordinates are
lengths, with $x^0=ct$ and $\partial_0=c^{-1}\partial_t$; $E_i$ has units
$\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and $B_i$ has units tesla.

Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as stated in [A2] and the adopted
curved vacuum Maxwell equations in [A1] on $\mathcal D$, with $\nabla$ the
Levi-Civita connection of $g$. A **point-normal
Lorentz chart at $p\in\mathcal D$** means a positively oriented chart in
$\mathcal D$ with $g_{ab}(p)=\operatorname{diag}
(-1,1,1,1)$, $\partial_cg_{ab}(p)=0$, and coordinate time axis $n(p)$.
In this chart define $\widehat E_i(x):=-cF_{0i}(x)$ and
$\widehat B_i(x):=\tfrac12\varepsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}(x)$; at $p$ these are the
components measured by $n(p)$. Derivatives in the pointwise formulas below
act on these chart-component functions, not on components of a varying
observer congruence. Then
$\nabla_a j^a=0$. At each event $p$, in a positively oriented point-normal
Lorentz chart whose time axis is $n(p)$, the component equations at $p$ are

$$\nabla\cdot\widehat{\mathbf E}=\rho/\epsilon_0,\qquad \nabla\times\widehat{\mathbf B}-c^{-2}\partial_t\widehat{\mathbf E}=\mu_0\mathbf J,\qquad \nabla\cdot\widehat{\mathbf B}=0,\qquad \partial_t\widehat{\mathbf B}+\nabla\times\widehat{\mathbf E}=0.$$

These four component equations hold throughout a fixed Minkowski inertial
chart with constant observer $n=\partial_0$. For $k\ge0$, let
$\Delta^k:=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_k)\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,\sum_i t_i=1\}$.
A **smooth singular $k$-simplex** is a smooth map $\Delta^k\to\mathcal D$; a
**finite smooth singular $k$-chain** is a finite real linear combination of
such simplices, with boundary the alternating sum of their oriented faces. A
smooth singular three-simplex is **spacelike** when its differential has rank
three and its pullback metric is positive definite on its interior; a
spacelike three-chain has this property on each simplex and is oriented by
its future-directed unit normal. For a finite smooth oriented spacelike
three-chain $\Sigma$ in the field domain, define its source charge by
$Q(\Sigma):=c^{-1}\int_\Sigma i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$ (in coulombs). If
$\partial\Sigma$ is its finite smooth boundary chain, then

$$Q(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{\mu_0c}\int_{\partial\Sigma}*F.$$

The component identities at a general event are local observer measurements;
they do not assert that an arbitrary observer field supplies a global inertial
coordinate system or a preferred foliation.
items.physical_scope: Conditional deduction of observer-frame SI Maxwell components, smooth-current conservation, and finite-chain Gauss flux in the adopted curved vacuum Maxwell model. It excludes singular or distributional sources, global component formulas for arbitrary non-inertial observers, and noncompact asymptotic charge claims; it reports no experiment or measurement.

items.title: Global Gauss flux and compact-slice neutrality
items.statement:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth ($C^\infty$), Hausdorff, second-countable,
boundaryless, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, with oriented metric volume form $\mathrm{vol}_g$. Use SI
constants $c>0$ with exact defining value $299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
and $\mu_0>0$ in $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ (experimentally determined in the
revised SI); define $\epsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{F\,m^{-1}}$.
Let $\mathcal D\subseteq M$ be the open field domain. Let $F$ be a smooth real
two-form with components in tesla and let $j$ be a smooth current vector field
with components in $\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}$ on $\mathcal D$. Assume
Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as
stated in [A2] and the adopted Maxwell equations in [A1]. A
For $k\ge0$, let $\Delta^k:=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_k)\in\mathbb R^{k+1}:t_i\ge0,
\sum_i t_i=1\}$. A **smooth singular $k$-simplex** is a smooth map
$\Delta^k\to\mathcal D$, and a **finite smooth singular $k$-chain** is a
finite real linear combination of such simplices; $\partial$ is the
alternating sum of their oriented faces. A smooth singular three-simplex is
**spacelike** when
its differential has rank three and its pulled-back metric is positive
definite on its interior; a spacelike three-chain has this property on each
simplex. Orient spacelike simplices using their future-directed unit normal.
Define insertion by
$(i_j\omega)(X_1,\ldots,X_{k-1})=\omega(j,X_1,\ldots,X_{k-1})$. For every
finite smooth singular three-chain $C$, set
$\Phi_j(C):=c^{-1}\int_C i_j\mathrm{vol}_g$; for a spacelike slice $\Sigma$
write $Q(\Sigma):=\Phi_j(\Sigma)$, in coulombs.

For every finite smooth oriented four-chain $V$ whose boundary decomposes as
$\partial V=\Sigma_2-\Sigma_1+B$, where $\Sigma_1,\Sigma_2$ are finite
spacelike three-chains and $B$ is the finite side chain, the source-current
flux satisfies

$$Q(\Sigma_2)-Q(\Sigma_1)=-\Phi_j(B).$$

For every compact boundaryless oriented smooth spacelike slice $\Sigma$ in
the domain, represented by a finite smooth three-cycle,
$Q(\Sigma)=0$. For every finite smooth three-chain $W$,
$\int_{\partial W}F=0$; where $j=0$ throughout $W$,
$\int_{\partial W}*F=0$. These conclusions concern bounding surfaces. A
closed surface is **nonbounding in the field domain** when it is a finite
smooth two-cycle $C$ with no finite smooth three-chain $W$ in that domain such
that $C=\partial W$; no zero-flux conclusion is made for such a surface. The
field topology is the global real closed-form model of [F2]; an optional
normalized $U(1)$ connection sector with chosen flux normalization $\kappa_0$
is extra structure, where $U(1):=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ under multiplication,
and no electric-charge quantization is inferred. For $b\ne0$ with $b$ in
webers and for each radius $r>0$ take
$\mathcal D=\mathbb R_{x^0}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$ with
$x^0=ct$, metric $g=-(dx^0)^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2$, standard orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx\wedge dy\wedge dz$, and
$r=(x^2+y^2+z^2)^{1/2}$; the Cartesian coordinates $x,y,z$ and $r$ are in
metres. The smooth two-form
$F_b=b(x\,dy\wedge dz+y\,dz\wedge dx+z\,dx\wedge dy)/r^3$ with $j=0$ is a
source-free solution, and the sphere $S^2_r$ at fixed $x^0$ has
$\int_{S^2_r}F_b=4\pi b\ne0$. Its Hodge-dual source-free field $- *F_b$ has
$\int_{S^2_r}* (-*F_b)=4\pi b\ne0$ as well. The sphere is nonbounding in
this punctured domain; this example makes no claim about a source or field
value at the excluded origin.
items.physical_scope: Finite-domain charge and flux identities under the smooth curved vacuum Maxwell postulate, including side-flux balance and neutrality of compact boundaryless smooth slices. Noncompact decay, singular boundaries, and empirical claims are outside scope; nonbounding cycles are not assigned zero flux by Stokes.

items.title: Pure electric and magnetic observer stress
items.statement:
Let $p$ be an event in an open neighborhood $U$ on which a smooth
future-directed unit timelike observer field $n$ is defined. At $p$ choose a
positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with time vector $n(p)$ and signature
$(-,+,+,+)$. Let $E_0\in\mathbb R$ have units $\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ and
$B_0\in\mathbb R$ have units tesla. For the pure-electric
observer field $\mathbf E=(E_0,0,0)$, $\mathbf B=0$, the SI stress components
of [F1], with the stated Countable Choice background premise [A2], are

$$T^{00}=\frac{\epsilon_0E_0^2}{2},\qquad T^{0i}=0,\qquad (T^{ij})=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(-\frac{\epsilon_0E_0^2}{2}, \frac{\epsilon_0E_0^2}{2},\frac{\epsilon_0E_0^2}{2}\right).$$

For the pure-magnetic observer field $\mathbf E=0$,
$\mathbf B=(0,0,B_0)$, they are

$$T^{00}=\frac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0},\qquad T^{0i}=0,\qquad (T^{ij})=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0}, \frac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0},-\frac{B_0^2}{2\mu_0}\right).$$

In each case $T^a{}_a=0$. The entries display anisotropic spatial stress in the
chosen observer frame; no perfect-fluid identification is made.
items.physical_scope: Pointwise algebraic computation of the pure-electric and pure-magnetic observer components of the adopted SI electromagnetic stress tensor, conditional on the planned stress-component lemma. It is not a global field solution or measured result.
